transcript.text: Chloe, you said something's been catching when you bite on the bottom right?
Yeah, the old filling on that back tooth — it feels like food keeps getting stuck around it.
Any sensitivity to cold or sweet at all?
A tiny bit of cold sensitivity, but it goes away quickly.

Sensibility: tooth 46 responds within normal limits to cold, no lingering response. No tenderness to percussion. Radiograph shows a defective distal margin with caries beneath the existing DO composite.

I can see the old filling on tooth four six has a cracked margin with decay underneath it — that's why things are getting stuck. The nerve is still healthy, so we'll replace the filling today rather than needing a root canal.
Good, I'd rather not go through that.

I'll isolate the tooth with a rubber dam, remove the old composite and the decay — the cavity is into dentine but not near the pulp — then place a new composite filling, shade A2, to match your other teeth. That's item 511 for the two-surface filling.
I'll check the bite with articulating paper to make sure there are no high spots, and polish it smooth. While the numbness lasts, be careful chewing on that side for a couple of hours.
A little sensitivity in the first few days is normal; if it lingers beyond that, give us a call. Otherwise I'll see you at your routine recall in six months.
